Wildlife Exploration · Yeovil

📷 Wildlife Camera Planner

Choose a calm, sensible place for a wildlife camera, predict what might visit, then record and analyse biodiversity changes over time.

Learning objective: I can create a mini-conservation area and record/analyse changes in biodiversity.

1 · Choose your route

You do not have to do this in order. Pick one small step, then the next. There are no timed questions and no wrong first ideas.

Today you are the wildlife survey team. Your job is to plan where a camera could collect useful observation data without disturbing people or wildlife.

2 · Place the camera

Tap the school grounds map to place your camera. You can move it as many times as you like.

Dashed areas are useful survey zones: woodland edge, field margin, path edge and quieter green spaces. Avoid aiming cameras at roads, car parks, windows or places where people gather.

Camera spot

No camera placed yet.

Safe & respectful survey

  • Ask an adult before placing the camera.
  • Point it at animal routes, not people routes.
  • Do not use bait unless staff agree.
  • Check recordings with a trusted adult.

3 · Explain your camera plan

Pick the clues that make your camera location useful. Choose only the ones that fit your idea.

Sentence starter: “I chose this place because it is near…, so the camera might record…”

4 · Build a mini-conservation area

Choose habitat features that could increase biodiversity near the camera. Tap again to remove.

Predicted visitors

This is a prediction, not a promise. Real observation data may surprise us.

Choose one habitat feature to see possible visitors.

5 · Record observation data

Use the log to record wildlife seen on the camera. You can add real data later, or practise with sample data now.
